items.title: Unity-Based Algorithm For Seamless Dungeon Generation
items.excerpt: A developer shared the Labyrinth Procedural Generator, a Unity algorithm that stitches dungeon rooms into seamless, playable layouts, with a live demo to try. Learn how the Labyrinth Procedural Generator works and try the demo.
items.why: Concrete procedural level-design craft: shows what generation actually buys a designer versus hand-authored layout, and where the seams have to be designed.

items.title: Unity's Stylized Water 3 Is Getting Spline-Based River Modeler Tool
items.excerpt: Stylized Water 3 is adding a spline-driven river modeler for Unity. It's designed around Burst and the Job System, features segmented river output, and automatic VFX/SFX integration.
items.why: Procedural authoring the designer still steers — a spline is the control surface. Useful counterpoint to prompt-first generation in environment art.

items.title: Breakdown: How Houdini Is Reshaping Commercial Animation
items.excerpt: Ezequiel Grand discussed how Houdini transformed his approach to commercial animation and VFX, explaining what pushed him to build a procedural house generator, and detailing six tips for building efficient procedural setups.
items.why: A working artist's account of moving from hand-built assets to procedural systems — the same authoring shift generative tools are forcing on game art teams.

items.title: Thanks to a dedicated team 'art-directing' every single NPC, GTA 6 has over 10 times as many unique animations as GTA 5
items.excerpt: Rockstar put a dedicated team on art-directing every single NPC in GTA 6, producing over 600,000 unique animations — more than ten times GTA 5's count.
items.why: The loudest counter-argument to generative NPCs right now: Rockstar bought crowd believability with human art direction at absurd scale, not a model.

items.title: A native port of Donkey Kong 64 is finally playable on PC thanks to programmers who boast that 'no generative AI was used at any point in the process'
items.excerpt: An unofficial native port of the classic Nintendo platformer now runs on modern hardware, and the decompilation team led with an explicit no-generative-AI disclaimer.
items.why: 'No AI was used' has become a craft credential you advertise up front — a signal of how disclosure norms are inverting in technical game work.

items.title: 'Claude Strife': DLSS 5 has escaped into the wild, and things are immediately weird
items.excerpt: With leaked DLSS 5 running on unreleased hardware, modders are seeing the generative tech restyle familiar characters. The controversial generative AI tech can look alright when used subtly, but the 'AI look' seems to be inescapable.
items.why: A neural renderer overriding a game's art direction at runtime is a new kind of design problem: who owns the look when the GPU repaints it?

items.title: GeForce RTX 3080 Drops From 138 FPS to 4 FPS When DLSS 5 Neural Rendering is Enabled
items.excerpt: DLSS 5 Neural Rendering runs on RTX 30 series but suffers a 97% FPS drop, making it unplayable, while RTX 50 series officially supports it.
items.why: The hard budget line for neural rendering: an AI look that costs 97% of your frame rate is a design constraint, not a feature toggle.

items.title: Modder Makes NVIDIA DLSS 5 Neural Rendering Work On GeForce RTX 40 Series Through A Simple CUDA Binaries Swap
items.excerpt: Modders enabled NVIDIA DLSS 5 Neural Rendering on RTX 40 GPUs via a CUDA binary swap, achieving up to 39% performance reduction in games like Control.
items.why: Generative graphics is being pried open by modders before it ships — the visual layer of games is becoming user-modifiable in a way art directors can't gate.

items.title: After AI backlash, Assassin's Creed creator says 1666: Amsterdam "won't be using any AI anymore"
items.excerpt: Patrice Desilets' studio says AI was only used "in conception and pre-production" on 1666: Amsterdam and will not be used going forward. Human-made magic only, please.
items.why: The emerging industry compromise — AI is tolerated in ideation but must be scrubbed from shipped assets — stated plainly by a marquee designer.

items.title: Three Epic veterans are building an AI-powered game engine to break the industry's doom cycle
items.excerpt: Amid mounting discontent with Unity and Unreal, new engine Immens promises lower costs and faster development for small teams, built by three former Epic engineers.
items.why: If the engine itself is AI-native, the whole authoring surface designers work on changes — this is the tooling layer, not another asset generator.

items.title: The Hollywood disruptors making a large-scale game with a 12-person team – and no generative AI
items.excerpt: The co-founders of Wolf Haus explain how Hollywood heritage and in-house tech came together to build cult simulator Join Us with a dozen people and zero generative AI.
items.why: Direct test of the 'AI is how small teams scale' claim — this team scaled with custom tooling and process instead, and says so.

items.title: Nvidia announces ray-traced Nanite, native anti-cheat, and DLSS 4.5 at Gamescom 2026
items.excerpt: Nvidia used Gamescom to detail a wave of developer-facing updates across DLSS, RTX, and its GeForce Now cloud platform.
items.why: Developer-facing pipeline changes: ray-traced Nanite and DLSS 4.5 reset what an art team can budget for geometry and lighting.

items.title: We're finally talking about AI, ft. David 'Rez' Graham and Luke Dicken
items.excerpt: Former Maxis engineer David "Rez" Graham and ex-Take-Two AI head Dr. Luke Dicken discuss AI and AI techniques in game development — a conversation about the nature of work and the inherent value of AI, not just the hype.
items.why: Two career game-AI practitioners separating classic game AI craft from generative hype — the vocabulary designers need to argue about this well.

items.title: Penguin Colony gave me a genAI fright in its release date trailer, but thankfully there's no actual cause for concern
items.excerpt: A cosmic-horror penguin sim's release trailer set off the writer's AI-detection instincts — wrongly. Fool me once, shame on me.
items.why: The false-positive cost of AI suspicion now lands on human artists whose style reads as 'generated' — a real reputational risk for stylised game art.

items.title: Nvidia DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction, out now, ups shadow quality and more accurately illuminates trash bags
items.excerpt: Nvidia have revealed DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction, an upgraded version of their path tracing cleaning-up tech, which is available today.
items.why: The uncontroversial half of neural graphics: a denoiser that lets lighting artists ship path tracing they could not previously afford.

items.title: Twitch faces a class action lawsuit over using streamers' content to train Amazon's AI
items.excerpt: Twitch content creator Warren Pandiscia has filed a proposed class action against Twitch and Amazon, alleging the companies used streamers' content to train AI.
items.why: Creator-made game content as training data without consent — the same fight that will hit anyone whose work lives on a platform they don't own.

items.title: DDoS Attack Breaks Beloved Video Game Wiki After AI Bro Was Banned
items.excerpt: The Cutting Room Floor wiki went offline after a DDoS attack allegedly triggered by a contributor banned for using Claude Code. The site had already deployed anti-AI defenses, including MS Paint warnings served to scrapers.
items.why: Game-history archives are hardening against AI agents; the reference material designers rely on is becoming a contested, defended resource.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Is at Least 10 Years Ahead of the Industry With NPCs, Says IOI's AI Programmer
items.excerpt: IO Interactive AI programmer Berkay Dursun broke down the crowds of Grand Theft Auto 6 in a series of posts, arguing 007 First Light doesn't come close.
items.why: A rival studio's AI programmer reading GTA 6's crowd systems in public — a rare technical breakdown of what 'good NPC AI' means as a design outcome.

items.title: NVIDIA's DLSS 5 has been leaked, and modders produced hideous faces and awful performance drops in its wake
items.excerpt: Early DLSS 5 builds pulled from game files are producing distorted character faces and heavy frame-rate losses in modder tests. Cloud, is that you?
items.why: Character faces are where generative upscaling breaks first — the exact place players read authorial intent, and where the tech's limits are most visible.

items.title: The AI paradox: why mobile embraces AI and triple-A holds back
items.excerpt: At PGC Summit Shanghai, studio leaders and investors asked why free-to-play races to adopt AI while AAA holds back, tracing the split to production risk and audience expectation.
items.why: Explains the split adoption curve by production model rather than ideology — useful frame for any design org deciding how fast to move. (Off-list outlet: no on-list source covered the mobile-vs-AAA adoption split this window.)
